old:
The **pretérito perfecto de subjuntivo** is formed by combining the present subjunctive of *haber* with the past participle:

• **haber**: *haya, hayas, haya, hayamos, hayáis, hayan*
• **participio**: *-ado* (hablado), *-ido* (vivido)
• **Irregular participles**: *dicho, hecho, puesto, visto, escrito, vuelto, abierto, roto*.

It refers to completed past actions connected to present attitudes, feelings, or doubts.
new:
You know the present perfect (*pretérito perfecto*: *he hablado*, *has vivido*) from A2 Unit 1 and the present subjunctive (*hable*, *vivas*) from A2 Unit 27. The **pretérito perfecto de subjuntivo** puts them together: the present subjunctive of *haber* plus the past participle you already know.

• **haber**: *haya, hayas, haya, hayamos, hayáis, hayan*
• **participio**: *-ado* (*hablado*), *-ido* (*vivido*)
• **Irregular participles** do not change: *dicho, hecho, puesto, visto, escrito, vuelto, abierto, roto*.

It follows the same triggers as the present subjunctive (feelings, doubt) when the action is already finished.
why: recap: pretérito perfecto (A2 Unit 1) and present subjunctive (A2 Unit 27) are known

old:
When expressing present feelings or value judgments about an action that already happened, use the present perfect subjunctive:

• *Me alegro de que hayas venido.* (I am glad you came / have come.)
• *Siento mucho que no hayas aprobado el examen.* (I am sorry you didn't pass the exam.)
• *Es fantástico / una lástima que hayan tomado esa decisión.* (It is fantastic / a pity that they made that decision.)
new:
You know the subjunctive after feelings and value judgments (*me alegro de que…*, *es una lástima que…*) from A2 Unit 27. When the event has already happened, the feeling stays in the present and the verb becomes *haya* + participle:

• *Me alegro de que hayas venido.* (I am glad you came / have come.)
• *Siento mucho que no hayas aprobado el examen.* (I am sorry you didn't pass the exam.)
• *Es fantástico / una lástima que hayan tomado esa decisión.* (It is fantastic / a pity that they made that decision.)
why: recap: feelings + subjunctive known from A2 Unit 27

old:
When you doubt or deny an event that supposedly already occurred in the past, use the present perfect subjunctive:

• *Dudo que hayan terminado todo el trabajo.* (I doubt they finished all the work.)
• *No creo que Juan haya dicho semejante cosa.* (I don't think Juan said such a thing.)
• *No es verdad que hayamos perdido los billetes.* (It's not true that we lost the tickets.)
• *¿Crees que haya salido ya el tren?* (Do you think the train has left already?)
new:
You know *dudo que* and *no creo que* + subjunctive from B1 Unit 13 and B1 Unit 25. To doubt or deny something that has already happened, use *haya* + participle:

• *Dudo que hayan terminado todo el trabajo.* (I doubt they finished all the work.)
• *No creo que Juan haya dicho semejante cosa.* (I don't think Juan said such a thing.)
• *No es verdad que hayamos perdido los billetes.* (It's not true that we lost the tickets.)
• *Es posible que haya salido ya el tren.* (The train may have left already.)
why: recap; ¿Crees que + subjunctive is not standard: replaced by es posible que

old:
The present perfect subjunctive can also refer to an action that will be completed *prior to another future event*:

• **cuando**: *Te llamo cuando haya terminado de cocinar.* (I'll call you when I have finished cooking.)
• **en cuanto / tan pronto como**: *En cuanto hayamos aterrizado, os mandaremos un mensaje.* (As soon as we have landed, we'll send you a message.)
• **después de que**: *Saldremos después de que haya dejado de llover.* (We will go out after it has stopped raining.)
new:
You know *cuando* and *en cuanto* + present subjunctive for future events from A2 Unit 27 (*Te llamo cuando termine*). When the first action must be finished before the second one, use *haya* + participle:

• **cuando**: *Te llamo cuando haya terminado de cocinar.* (I'll call you when I have finished cooking.)
• **en cuanto / tan pronto como**: *En cuanto hayamos llegado a casa, te mandaré un mensaje.* (As soon as we have got home, I'll send you a message.)
• **with a command**: *Llámame cuando hayas terminado.* (Call me when you have finished.)

old:
Mastering the subjunctive at B1 requires choosing between current/future actions vs completed past actions:

• **Present Subjunctive** (*hables, vengas*): Refers to simultaneous or future events:
  *Espero que vengas a mi fiesta mañana.* (I hope you come tomorrow.)
• **Present Perfect Subjunctive** (*hayas hablado, hayas venido*): Refers to completed events:
  *Espero que hayas venido en metro.* (I hope you came by metro.)
• Contrast: *Dudo que lo hagan hoy* (future action) vs. *Dudo que lo hayan hecho ya* (completed action).
new:
You know the present subjunctive (*vengas*, *hables*) from A2 Unit 27, and the first lessons of this unit gave you the perfect form (*hayas venido*). The choice between them is a choice of time:

• **Present subjunctive** (*vengas*): the action is happening now or is still to come: *Espero que vengas a mi fiesta mañana.* (I hope you come to my party tomorrow.)
• **Present perfect subjunctive** (*hayas dormido*): the action is already finished: *Espero que hayas dormido bien.* (I hope you slept well.)
• Contrast: *Dudo que lo hagan hoy* (a future action) and *Dudo que lo hayan hecho ya* (a finished action).
why: recap A2 Unit 27 + this unit; "hayas venido en metro" was odd
